Digital is the electronics of counting. By comparing numbers, it's possible to turn on a light, sound an alarm or make a TV operate.

Early man kept track of objects by counting with his fingers......
However, this method reached a limit at the number 10...........
The Chinese made a tool called the Abacus. The Abacus was the first digital counting device.
The abacus is capable of counting, addition, subtraction, multiplication and division...
In the 17th century, the abacus was improved by a mechanical counting machine built by a Frenchman named Pascal.
In the 19th century an Englishman named Babbage made the mechanical counting machine work with a Programmed Controller.
ENTERPAGE
The real advances in digital counting devices occurred in 1940 with the development of the ENIAC computer.
The ENIAC was the first generation of the modern digital computer. It used vacuum tubes that were big, expensive and unreliable.
The second generation of digital computers replaced the vacuum tube with the transistor. The transistor was small, inexpensive and reliable.
The third generation of digital computer combined the transistor with new technology and created the integrated circuit (IC).
The integrated circuit contains many transistors.................
The computer is not the only use for digital electronics. There are many applications for digital circuits.
>DFFGMNNOR

Most consumer products use digital circuits or microprocessors to control their operation.

The signals applied to analog circuits are varying voltages or sine waves.
The output is an amplification of the input that varies depending on the design of the circuit.
Digital circuits are constructed from analog components, but their design makes them operate differently.
The most obvious difference is the digital circuit is represented by a box instead of actual components.
Another difference is digital circuits only react to two input signals or voltage levels.
The square or pulse waves are suited for digital circuits because they have instantaneous rise and fall times. Let's look closer at the two waveforms..........................
These two waveforms only have two conditions, HIGH at 5 volts and LOW at 0 volts.
These two waveforms only have two conditions, HIGH at 3 volts and LOW at 1 volt.
A digital circuit looks for the presence of a signal or the absence of a signal at its input.
If the square wave is HIGH the signal is present. If the square wave is LOW the signal is absent.

The terms AND, OR and NOT describe the logic functions performed...
LOGIC - The term logic is used in digital circuits to describe functions, operations or voltage levels.
DEFINITION
These three basic functions are used to construct all digital circuits. Let's start with the AND function.
The AND logic function produces a HIGH output ONLY if all the inputs are HIGH.
For example, your car's engine starts only if the ignition is on AND the battery has a charge.
This example is simplified by using a truth table.

The last function is the NOT function............................
The NOT logic function inverts the input signal, producing the opposite signal as the output.
DEFINITION
INVERTS - The term invert means that a signal is changed to the opposite condition. A TRUE signal becomes a FALSE signal. Ones become zeros, HIGHS become LOWS. The output is NOT the input.
The NOT function is used with the AND and OR functions to change their output when the opposite condition is needed.
In this example, the AND function produces a 1 output when all inputs are 1. The NOT function inverts the 1 to a 0.
The truth table for the NOT function is very simple..............
